sam: FYI ran apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic for long-context mixes. Initial notes below. TL;DR: prefill-dominant workloads show KV cache hits change tail latency, and kernel selection differences can swing throughput ~10-14% depending on seqlen mix.

anya: Nice — did you pin kernels/quant levels? what env?

sam: Dedicated bench node: a100-80gb, pytorch 2.2, runtime hash abc123, model gpt-medium-16k (fp16) and q4f16 variants. Pins: same kernel set for both runs. Commands used: ```./bench/run_replay --trace replay.json --clients 120 --duration 30m --seq_dist context_mix.yaml```

kevin: Can you share seq_dist? was it prefill-heavy or steady stream?

sam: Prefill-heavy: 60% prefill >8k tokens, 30% 512-2048 conv, 10% short. Short summary inline below.

maria: What about KV cache eviction behavior? Did you prime cache between requests?

sam: We used warmup phase: 5m ramp with identical distribution to prime KV on pinned worker. But note: replay preserves per-session KV; our synthetic harness by default reset cache per request — that explains the raw tail differences. After toggling synthetic to reuse session IDs, p95 latency dropped ~18% on the prefill-heavy run.

anya: Ah that explains it. Can we standardize session semantics for apples-to-apples? Replay should be 'session-preserving' to match real traffic.

sam: Agreed. Updated harness flag: `--session-policy preserve`. Also added `--session-seed` to reproduce deterministic cache priming.

bench-bot: bench-bot: new harness build v0.9.1 available at ci/bench/v0.9.1 :rocket:

kevin: What about kernel selection — did runtime pick different kernels for long prefill vs short conv?

sam: Yes. For long-prefill, compiler picks blocked attention kernels for large seqlen slices. For short convs it picked unrolled kernels. Observed 9-14% throughput delta between the two paths depending on chunking. We should surface seqlen-aware kernel choices in the profiler.

alex: Can you paste profiler snippet?

sam: Sure, snippet from trace:
```
[profiler] timeline: session=42 prefill 8192 -> kernel: blocked_attn_v2 (seq_chunk=2048) latency=78.3ms
[profiler] timeline: session=42 conv 256   -> kernel: unrolled_attn (seq_chunk=256) latency=3.2ms
[profiler] kernel_decision: avg_seqlen=1794 -> chosen=blocked_attn_v2 (est_throughput=12.3k toks/s)
[profiler] kernel_decision: avg_seqlen=320  -> chosen=unrolled_attn   (est_throughput=14.1k toks/s)
```

maria: Any perf regression vs last stable? We ran nightly on q4f16 and saw some variance.

sam: Compared to runtime v0.7.2: overall tokens/sec down ~6% on mixed load. Root cause: heuristic bug that overestimates blocked kernel efficiency for mid-range seqlen leading to more blocked kernels than optimal. Repro locally and in CI. Fix candidate in PR #284.

anya: Good catch. Is there a repro we can run?

sam: Yes: repro script: `scripts/repro/seqlen-heuristic-regress.sh --model gpt-medium-16k --mix config/context-mix-repro.yaml`. Reproduces in ~20m on a single pinned worker.

kevin: Let's schedule a quick patch: change heuristic threshold from 3.0x -> 2.2x chunk_size ratio and re-run apples-to-apples. Any objections?

maria: No objections. Also propose CI step that runs the apples-to-apples replay (session-preserving) as a regression test for seq-mix perf. Add baseline artifacts to catch throughput drops >5%.

sam: I'll open PR with the heuristic change, add the reproducible script, and attach benchmark artifacts (latency CSV, perf traces, kernel decision logs). Linking results after CI: ci/bench/artifacts/1771004321/. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
